observation_summary: The BrentSolver returns the function value (yMin or yMax) instead of the actual root (min or max) when one of the endpoints is a root.
hypothesis: The solver incorrectly assigns the function value (yMin/yMax) to the result variable instead of the endpoint (min/max) when the endpoint is identified as a root.
prediction: The code will show that the setResult method is called with yMin or yMax instead of min or max.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that the arguments to setResult were changed from yMin/yMax to min/max, confirming that the wrong value was being assigned as the result.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of assigning the wrong value to a variable. The logic to identify the root (the condition) is correct, but the value assigned to the result upon finding that root is incorrect (the function value instead of the input coordinate). This fits the definition of Assignment/Initialization.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The procedural logic for finding the root is correct; only the specific value assigned to the result variable is wrong.
The condition checking if the endpoint is a root is correct; the issue is what happens after the condition is met.
